item: V4-STORAGEDEADLINE-001; revised by BUG-SWEETPOTATODEADLINE-001, then corrected by the 2026-08-17 crucible (D3/D4)
note: Per-CROP-TYPE seasonal LIFT deadlines for 'single'-habit storage crops — the crops isReadyToPick() structurally cannot surface (harvestReadiness.js requires harvest_habit IN ('repeat','cut_and_come_again') AND >=1 prior harvest, so every once-per-season crop is invisible to the ready band). Keyed by crop_types.slug, same key space as harvest-attributes-v1.json. THIS FILE IS DELIBERATELY ALMOST EMPTY. A date with no citable source is not a date; the disconfirmations in `no_calendar_deadline` are as load-bearing as the one record in `by_crop_type` and exist so the next session does not re-derive the falsified premise from scratch.
provenance_rule: Every entry in by_crop_type carries source + source_url + confidence, and its `true_trigger` names the physical signal the calendar date is only a PROXY for. Where the trigger is an observed plant state the app does not record, the crop belongs in no_calendar_deadline, NOT in by_crop_type with an invented date. ADDED 1.2.0: where the DATE itself is not a phrase the cited source states — i.e. anything other than `regional_calendar_proxy` — the record MUST carry a `measured_basis` with a reproducible query, or it is a rationale wearing a number. Precedent for the harm: harvestWindows.json shipped at 11.8% cultivar calibration with 22-day median error, and this file's own sweet-potato date was moved twice on two different confident rationales before anyone measured the site.
frost_anchor_warning: FROST_ANCHORS.firstFallFrost (src/lib/sowEngine.js, '09-28') is a CONSERVATIVE SOWING-SAFETY MARGIN, not an observed frost date, and NO deadline in this file may be derived from it — not as an offset, not as a bound, not as a tiebreak. Measurement at this exact site (see any record's `measured_basis`): the first <=32F night has never fallen before 10-10 in 11 years and its median is 10-29, so the anchor sits 12 to 41 days ahead of frost that has actually occurred. That conservatism is right for its own job (deciding whether a sowing can finish) and wrong as a harvest cutoff, because a harvest cutoff pulled early forfeits certain bulking weeks against a hazard that has not materialised. This file has now derived its sweet-potato date from the anchor TWICE and been wrong both times, in opposite directions: 1.0.0 put it at anchor+17d on a soil-temperature reading, 1.1.0 at anchor-3d on a vine-kill reading. The vine-kill MECHANISM is correct and survives (see true_trigger); the anchor-relative DATE was the error both times. 1.2.0 derives the date from measurement instead, and storageDeadlines.test.js now pins deadlines to `measured_basis` rather than to the anchor. Also do NOT blanket-derive every crop from any frost date — the frost-tolerant roots in no_calendar_deadline correctly have no frost deadline at all.

field_contract.deadline_kind: Exactly two kinds are defined; do not invent a third. `regional_calendar_proxy` = a calendar date a regional extension source states as the practical cutoff, standing in for a physical trigger the app cannot measure. `measured_site_backstop` = a date computed from a reproducible measurement AT THIS SITE, chosen as the last-resort catch for the year nobody watched the forecast — NOT a prediction of when the trigger will fire, and NOT to be re-argued as a derived optimum. A `measured_site_backstop` is invalid without `measured_basis`.
field_contract.deadline_month_day: MM-DD. Resolved against the year of the caller-supplied today, never against an internal clock.
field_contract.check_from_month_day: MM-DD the CHECK window opens. Always earlier than deadline_month_day. The gap is deliberate lead time, not a second deadline.
field_contract.true_trigger: The physical signal the date proxies for. Prose, for display and for honesty — the date is downstream of this, not the other way round.
field_contract.measured_basis: REQUIRED on any `measured_site_backstop`. The measurement the date is computed from, recorded so the NEXT session can re-run it in one command and get a number back instead of re-reading a rationale. Must carry: `query` (a complete, executable request — coordinates, variable, units, timezone, date span), `source` + `source_url`, `years`, and the derived statistics with their field names. If a claim in here cannot be reproduced from `query`, the field is decoration and the date is unsourced.
field_contract.on_frost_action: REQUIRED where true_trigger is a weather EVENT rather than a plant state. What to do the day the event is forecast — the date is only the backstop for the year this was missed.
field_contract.cure: Post-lift handling, where a correct lift date followed by wrong handling loses the crop just as completely. Must agree with harvestWindows.json for the same crop; the two are cross-checked in test.
field_contract.loss: What is actually lost, and when it becomes visible. Storage-crop loss materialises months later in the pantry, which is why it needs surfacing at all.
field_contract.check_copy / past_copy: User-facing copy. CHECK FORM ONLY — 'start checking X', never 'X is ready'. These estimates are weak and the copy must not overclaim.
field_contract.confidence: high | medium | low. medium = a regional extension source states the guidance, but as a typical case ('usually before...'), not a measured threshold.

sweet_potato.true_trigger: Vine kill, not soil temperature. Frost blackens the vines well before the soil cools, and once the vines are dead the roots begin degrading in the ground — decay enters through the crown and the roots will not store, however warm the soil still is. The published soil thresholds (growth stops below 65F, chilling injury below 55F) are real but they are not what closes the window first in 5b. THE TRIGGER IS THE FORECAST, NOT THE CALENDAR: the date below is only the backstop for a year in which nobody watched it.

measured_basis.what: First fall night at or below 32F at this site — the event that kills the vines and starts the clock in true_trigger.
measured_basis.query: GET https://archive-api.open-meteo.com/v1/archive?latitude=42.5087&longitude=-72.6471&start_date=2015-09-01&end_date=2025-11-30&daily=temperature_2m_min&temperature_unit=fahrenheit&timezone=America%2FNew_York — then, per year, the first date with temperature_2m_min <= 32.
measured_basis.source: Open-Meteo historical reanalysis archive (ERA5), 2m minimum air temperature
measured_basis.september_bounds: ZERO September nights <=36F in 11 years, and zero <=32F. Coldest September night in the whole record is 38.2F (2019-09-19). Only 4 September nights <=40F across all 11 years (38.2, 38.2, 38.5, 40.0), none earlier than 09-19. The first-frost distribution's left tail does not reach September at all, which is what falsified the 1.1.0 date of 09-25.
measured_basis.instrument_limits: ERA5 is a ~9km grid and does not resolve a 518ft hilltop; canopy surface temperature on calm radiational nights runs 3-5F below 2m air. Applying a full 5F cold offset to the coldest September on record still yields ~33F, on 4 nights in 11 years, none before 09-19 — so the offset does not move the conclusion. It DOES mean 10-10 could arrive as a canopy event a few days before the 2m record shows it, which is the reason to treat 10-10 as a backstop and act on the forecast instead.
measured_basis.reproduced_by: horticulture-planning-analyst seat, then boss-technical, then this implementation lane — three independent re-runs, identical row for row (2026-08-17).

sweet_potato.on_frost_action: On ANY frost forecast, at any date: cut the vines at the soil line that day, and dig within 24-48h. Severing the vines stops decay travelling down into the crown, which is what makes a late backstop safe at all. Do not wait for the calendar date if frost is forecast before it.
sweet_potato.cure: 80-85F at 85-90% relative humidity for 5-10 days (or 2-3 weeks at 65-75F), single layer in flats, do not wash and do not pile. Then 55-60F in the dark, never below 55F — refrigeration causes the same chilling injury as cold soil. Curing is where starch converts to sugar, so an uncured root is starchy and a cured one is sweet; a correct lift date followed by no cure loses the crop as completely as a late lift. Matches harvestWindows.json by_crop_type.sweet_potato, which is the same guidance in on-screen form.
sweet_potato.loss: The whole stored crop, invisible at harvest. Roots left in after vine kill rot from the crown; chilled roots show shrivelled, sunken, dark areas and blacken when cut, and 'hardcore' roots stay hard after cooking. The damage is permanent and only shows up in storage.
sweet_potato.check_copy: Start checking sweet potatoes for lifting — frost kills the vines and the roots begin degrading the moment it does, so they want to be out of the ground before the first one. Watch the forecast: if frost is coming, cut the vines at the soil line that day and dig within 48 hours. The earliest frost measured here in 11 years is October 10th, so treat that as the backstop.
sweet_potato.past_copy: Sweet potato lifting window has passed — worth checking whether any are still in the ground.
sweet_potato.source: UMass Extension — Sweet Potato Harvest and Storage (mechanism and cure); the DATE is from measured_basis, not from this source
sweet_potato.notes: 10-10 is a BACKSTOP, not a derived date and not a prediction — it is the earliest first-<=32F night in 11 years of measurement at this exact site (measured_basis), i.e. the earliest date frost has EVER killed the vines here. Median first frost is 10-29, so in a typical year this leaves ~19 days of bulking unclaimed, and that gap IS the safety margin. It is a min-of-sample and will move if the record grows; that is acceptable for a backstop and is NOT acceptable as a derived optimum, so do not re-argue it as one. SUPERSEDES 1.1.0's 09-25, which was FROST_ANCHORS.firstFallFrost - 3d and fired 15-44 days before frost has ever occurred here, forfeiting the highest-rate storage-root bulking weeks every single year against a hazard whose distribution has no September tail. 1.1.0's vine-kill MECHANISM was right and is retained unchanged — the date was the error, and only the date reverts. Also supersedes 1.0.0's 10-15, which landed within 5 days of the right answer by soil-temperature reasoning that was itself wrong: a right number from a wrong mechanism, which is why the 1.1.0 session was able to move it confidently. WHAT WOULD FALSIFY THIS: a storage-quality or loss disposition recorded against a lifted crop. None exists in the schema today (38 event types, no spoilage/discard), so no evidence about this date will accumulate in January 2027 unless that ships — see the crucible's C8 deferral. Dave has 2 live sweet potato plantings (verified live prod 2026-08-17), both status 'vegetative'.

no_calendar_deadline._note: Crops examined for V4-STORAGEDEADLINE-001 and deliberately NOT given a date. Each records WHY and what signal would have to exist first. Removing a crop from this list requires a citable regional source, not a plausible guess.

winter_squash.design_claim: 'off the vine before frost touches fruit or it will not store'
winter_squash.finding: Not supported by the regional source, and the trigger is not a date at all. The UMass pumpkin/winter-squash fact sheet gives no frost or freeze guidance; its 50F threshold is CHILLING INJURY IN STORAGE, a post-harvest condition, which also means 'cold storage' is the wrong destination for this crop. Penn State puts field damage at a HARD FREEZE below 28F — materially colder and later than 'frost'. The binding constraint is FRUIT MATURITY, not vine state and not soil: (1) a rind that resists a thumbnail, (2) the ground spot turned cream or orange, (3) an intact ~2in stem handle, since a broken peduncle is the single largest storage-rot entry point. The app already states cue (1) correctly at src/lib/ripenessCues.js. Frost that kills the VINES stops further rind hardening but does not ruin sound fruit; frost landing on exposed fruit tissue is what admits rot. So the right prompt on a frost forecast is 'cut the mature fruit, leave the immature' — a conditional on an observed state, not a calendar cutoff. REJECTED EXPLICITLY 2026-08-17: a pre-frost vine-kill deadline copied from sweet potato's mechanism. Sweet potato's harvest is a ROOT whose decay pathway runs down the killed vine; winter squash's harvest is a fruit already detached from that pathway. Same family of reasoning, opposite conclusion. Cure regime, which is species-split and has no calendar in it either: C. moschata (butternut) cures 80-85F at 80-85% RH for 10-14 days; C. maxima (hubbard, kabocha, buttercup) generally should NOT be warm-cured; C. pepo acorn types must NOT be cured at all — curing shortens their storage life. Store 50-55F. Still moot operationally: 0 live winter_squash plantings in prod (re-verified 2026-08-17).
winter_squash.needed: Nothing for a deadline — this crop correctly has none, and the disconfirmation is now twice-tested. What IS outstanding is an ATTRIBUTE gap in a different dataset, recorded here because this is where the next session will look: `winter_squash` has existed as a real crop type since V4-CROPSPLIT-001 (live in prod, harvest_habit 'single', repeat_interval_days NULL — re-verified 2026-08-17), but `src/data/harvest-attributes-v1.json` by_crop_type and its generated seed `migrations/v4-harvattr-001/0b-data.sql` have no row for it, so prod `winter_squash.loss_horizon_hours` is NULL where `squash` carries 36. Consequences: no loss horizon for a butternut, and `0r-rollback.sql` regenerates attributes FROM that JSON, so rolling back v4-harvattr-001 would leave winter_squash permanently unattributed. harvestAttributesSync.test.js cannot catch this — it asserts JSON<->SQL equality between two repo files and never consults live crop_types, so a live crop type with no attributes row is invisible to it in both directions. Fix belongs to whoever owns harvest-attributes-v1.json, needs the both-envs migration gate, and should land before the 2027 winter-squash sowing named in expansion-crops-2027.

bean_dry.design_claim: 'in at pod-rattle before the next wetting'
bean_dry.finding: Dave does not grow dry beans. All 3 live `bean` plantings are snap/filet bush types (Contender, Gold Rush, Tavera), and crop_types.bean is harvest_habit='repeat' — so they are already visible to the ready-to-pick band and are not a storage crop at all. There is no dry-bean crop type.
bean_dry.needed: A dry-bean crop type and a live planting. The trigger (pod rattle) is an observed state the schema does not record.

garlic.design_claim: 'cure then move before humidity re-softens wrappers'
garlic.finding: Garlic is the ONE crop already carrying a hard window: crop_types.harvest_season_start_doy=186 / end_doy=211 = 2026-07-05 to 2026-07-30. That window closed before this item was filed. Zero garlic harvests have ever been logged, and the single live planting is still status 'vegetative'. A deadline feature cannot help 2026 garlic; it would fire on a window already 13 days shut. AMENDED 2026-08-26 (V4-GARLICANNUAL-001) — the two numbers quoted above are no longer current: the window is now 196/217 = Jul 15 - Aug 5, moved later because the generic zone-5b start opened too early for Dave's ridge. The finding itself still stands as written; only the citation moved. Two further facts recorded here because this entry is where a future reader looks: the planting is no longer 'vegetative' — it was set 'dormant' on 2026-08-13, with zero harvest ever logged, on the mistaken reasoning that garlic overwinters into a second year and bulbs up next spring, which is the model V4-GARLICANNUAL-001 corrects at crop_types.default_lifecycle. And the window remains INERT for garlic either way: isReadyToPick short-circuits on harvest_habit='single' before reading these columns, so nothing fires on them today, correct values or not.
garlic.needed: Nothing new for the harvest deadline — it exists. The CURING stage the claim is actually about is a post-harvest process with no schema representation at all.

onion.design_claim: 'lift within 10-14d of leaf-fall or necks rot and the crop will not store'
onion.finding: The trigger is leaf-fall (tops going over) — an OBSERVED PLANT STATE. There is no leaf_fall event type in event_log (38 types in prod, none of them this), so the 10-14 day clock has nothing to start from. A calendar substitute would be a guess. Separately, the premise that these close invisibly did not hold: Dave lifted onions on 07-27, 07-28 and 08-04 with no app prompt.
onion.needed: A leaf-fall / tops-down observation event type. Then the deadline is derived, not invented.

shallot.finding: Same unrecorded leaf-fall trigger. Same disconfirmation, more strongly: Dave lifted shallots on 07-23, 07-26, 07-30, 08-04 and 08-08 — five separate picks, incrementally, unprompted. The observed behaviour is continuous pulling as needed, not a single storage lift on a deadline.

cabbage.finding: The trigger is a rainfall EVENT crossed with head maturity. event_log has a `rain` type (723 rows) but no rainfall depth that would distinguish 'heavy' from any rain, and no head-maturity signal. This is a weather-reactive alert, not a seasonal deadline — it does not belong in a deadline dataset even once buildable. Cabbage is also frost-tolerant, so no fall date applies.
cabbage.needed: Rainfall depth on rain events plus a head-formed signal. Belongs to a weather-alert feature, not this one.

potato.finding: Examined and rejected, twice. UMass gives harvest conditions (soil 45-65F, tuber 50-60F) and a 10-14 day skin-set hold after vine kill, but NO calendar cutoff. Tubers are unharmed by the frost that kills the vines; the real limit is ground freeze, far later than first frost and not anchored anywhere in the app. The 10-14 day hold is also NOT unconditional, and the condition is the haulm — the clock runs from HAULM REMOVAL, never from frost-kill-in-place. Three branches: (a) healthy senesced haulm over dry soil — hold 10-14 days for skin set, as written; (b) frost-killed or lesioned haulm — remove the haulm off the bed IMMEDIATELY, then hold 10-14 days if the soil is dry, because a 2-week wait under dead blighted tops is how spores wash down onto the tubers; (c) dead haulm over saturated soil — dig now, cull, eat first, do not store. Post-lift, absent from the original record: cure 7-14 days at 50-60F and 85-95% RH, dark, and do not wash. REJECTED EXPLICITLY 2026-08-17: adding a frost-anchored deadline here by analogy with sweet potato. That analogy is false — sweet potato's root decays through the killed vine, a potato tuber does not — and acting on it would have put a wrong deadline on 3 live plantings. 3 live plantings (re-verified 2026-08-17).
potato.needed: Nothing for a deadline — this crop correctly has none. The conditional above is keyed on haulm condition, an observed plant state with no event type in prod; the same vine_kill / tops_down observation that would unblock onion, shallot and sweet potato is what would make it derivable. A ground-freeze anchor also does not exist; FROST_ANCHORS has no such field.

carrot.finding: Frost-tolerant and deliberately left in ground — extension guidance is to hold carrots in the soil UNTIL frost and harvest before the ground freezes. A first-frost deadline would be actively wrong: it would pull a crop that improves. 3 live plantings.
carrot.needed: Nothing. This crop correctly has no deadline.

beet.finding: Recovers from 1-2 light freezings; guidance is to harvest before the first MODERATE freeze or mulch for winter harvest. No first-frost deadline. Dave picked beets on 07-16, 07-31 (x2) and 08-04 unprompted. 2 live plantings.
beet.needed: Nothing. This crop correctly has no deadline.

leek.finding: The most frost-tolerant of the set — some varieties take temperatures near 20F, and delaying harvest past first frost is the recommended practice. crop_types.loss_horizon_hours=1440 (60 days) already encodes that it holds. 2 live plantings.
leek.needed: Nothing. This crop correctly has no deadline.
